before: Optional<String> holds a String or no value. Optional.ofNullable accepts a possibly null reference and produces an empty Optional for null. An empty string is still a present String.

isPresent tests presence; get requires a present value and otherwise throws NoSuchElementException. This explicit guard makes the example safe. Prefer APIs that clearly state whether absence is expected.

Optional.empty is not null and is not automatically an error. Do not use Optional itself as a null reference. Other combinators can transform values later; the present/absent distinction is the core here.

Optional.empty() takes no arguments and returns an Optional with no value; the generic String type describes what a present value would be:
```java
java.util.Optional<String> empty = java.util.Optional.empty();
System.out.println(empty.isPresent());
```
Output: false.

Expected output or behavior: missing

Optional local transfer task: Compare a null input, empty String and nonempty String without changing the guard. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Optional holds either a value or no value. Optional.ofNullable turns a null reference into an empty Optional. A real String, even one with no text, becomes a present value.
isPresent checks whether a value exists. get reads it, but throws NoSuchElementException if it is absent. The if check here ensures get runs only when a value is present.
Optional.empty means an Optional with no value inside. It is different from null, which points to no object. Keep the Optional itself present so its methods can describe whether its value is missing.
The program prints missing. result is an empty Optional, so get and length are skipped.
The quiz uses an empty String instead of null. The String is present, even though its length is zero.

before.question: Replace null with an empty String. Which branch runs?
choices: get throws because a String must contain letters
missing, because empty strings are absent
before.explanation: Presence depends on whether a value exists, not whether the value has positive length. An empty String is a present value.

after.question: Replace null with an empty String. Which branch runs?
choices: get throws because the String has no letters.
The missing branch runs because empty text is absent.
after.explanation: An empty String is a real value. isPresent returns true, get retrieves it, and length returns zero.
